title: Proximity-based proteomics reveals subcellular targeting sequence in Cyanobacteria
content: Cyanobacteria are oxygenic phototrophs that significantly contribute to the carbon and nitrogen cycles by producing O2 and fixing N2. Unlike most prokaryotes and gram-negative bacteria, cyanobacteria possess a distinctive intracellular organization that includes a plasma membrane (PM), a periplasm and outer membrane with a peptidoglycan layer in between, thylakoid membranes (TMs), and proteinaceous organelles like carboxysomes, which support the carbon-concentrating mechanism (Cameron et al. 2013; Dahlgren et al. 2021). These compartments contain unique proteins essential for various physiological functions, such as photosynthesis, carbon fixation, and nutrient transport; however, the mechanisms for targeting proteins to these locations have remained poorly understood.
